chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid, from Muhammad al-Asamm, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worthless ones of your deceased are the celibates (those who died unmarried).'

key_terms.الْعُزَّاب: Plural of 'azab' — celibates, unmarried persons; those who refrained from or died without marriage
key_terms.رُذَال: The plural of 'radhil' — meaning the vile, lowly, or worthless ones; the contemptible
key_terms.مَوْتَى: The deceased, the dead; those who have passed away

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about people who die unmarried according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) declared that those who die in a state of celibacy — without having married — are the most contemptible among the deceased. The statement strongly encourages marriage as a religious and social obligation, reflecting the Islamic emphasis on family formation as a means of spiritual and communal fulfillment. In the context of early Islamic society, dying unmarried was seen as a failure to fulfill a fundamental human and religious duty, leaving one without progeny and without fulfilling the sunnah of the Prophet.

en.hubeali:
And fromhim, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Al Samma, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The worthless ones of your deceased are the (ones who died as) celibates (unmarried)’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ali from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid from Muhammad al-Asamm who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘The worthless dead among you are the unmarried ones.’”
